checks.check: M/M/1: simulated mean wait within tolerance of the analytic Pollaczek-Khinchine value
M/D/1: simulated mean wait within tolerance of the analytic Pollaczek-Khinchine value
M/D/1 mean wait is lower than M/M/1 at equal load (service variance removed)

conclusion: hypothesis supported by all stated checks
falsifier: Either simulated mean wait falls outside three standard errors (with a five-percent relative floor) of its analytic value, or M/D/1 does not have the lower mean wait at equal load.
hypothesis: At utilisation 0.8 with Poisson arrivals of rate 0.8 and one server with mean service 1/1.0, the simulated mean wait in queue reproduces rho/(mu(1-rho)) = 4.0 for M/M/1 and rho/(2 mu(1-rho)) = 2.0 for M/D/1 within tolerance, and M/D/1's mean wait is lower.
limitation: Textbook queues only: Poisson arrivals, one server, exponential or constant service, unbounded capacity, FCFS discipline. This measures agreement between a simulation and the published formulas on that model; it is not a latency measurement of any real system.
method: 20 independent FCFS runs per model of 40000 customers each (Lindley recursion), first 4000 customers discarded as warm-up; standard error computed across trial means.
metric: mean wait in queue per customer
